summary: India's Bureau of Immigration says visa-free entry is available to citizens of Nepal, Bhutan and the Maldives; for others a valid passport and a regular visa, e-Visa or OCI card are required. Citizens of the countries and territories on India's e-Visa list can apply online for an e-Tourist Visa of one month, one year or five years; the portal's fee table gives each nationality's fee, and its FAQ says indianvisaonline.gov.in is the only official website to apply.

passportValidity.text: India's e-Visa instructions say the passport should have at least six months' validity at the time of applying for the e-Visa and at least two blank pages for stamping. The UK Foreign Office tells British nationals their passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after the date they arrive and at least 2 blank pages.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: India's Bureau of Immigration says anyone arriving from or transiting through a yellow fever endemic country by air or sea must hold a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate, and that foreigners or Indians (excluding infants below six months) arriving without one who have visited or transited such an area will be kept in quarantine for up to 6 days. It lists 30 notified endemic countries in Africa and 13 in South America.

source.name: Bureau of Immigration, India — Health Regulation

vaccinations.name: Polio (OPV/IPV)
vaccinations.text: WHO's country list says India requires proof of oral polio vaccination, taken at least 4 weeks before departure, from resident national travellers from polio-endemic countries (Afghanistan, Nigeria, Pakistan) and from countries with poliovirus circulation following importation (Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, Syria).

source.name: WHO — Vaccination requirements and recommendations for international travellers, country list (ITH 2022)

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for India. The UK Foreign Office advises checking before you travel that you have appropriate travel insurance for local treatment or unexpected medical evacuation.

source.name: UK FCDO — India travel advice: health

onwardTicket.text: India's e-Visa instructions say the foreigner should have a return ticket or onward journey ticket, with sufficient money to spend during the stay in India.

source.name: Indian Visa Online — e-Visa eligibility, instructions and FAQ (Bureau of Immigration)

proofOfFunds.text: India's e-Visa instructions say the foreigner should have a return ticket or onward journey ticket, with sufficient money to spend during the stay in India. No official source we could read states an amount.

source.name: Indian Visa Online — e-Visa eligibility, instructions and FAQ (Bureau of Immigration)

declarations.name: Designated eVisa entry points
declarations.text: The e-Visa portal says eVisa holders will be allowed to enter India only through the designated international airports (36 on its checkpoint list) and seaports listed on the e-Visa website.

source.name: Indian Visa Online — e-Visa eligibility, instructions and FAQ (Bureau of Immigration)

declarations.name: e-Arrival Card
declarations.text: India's visa portal says foreign nationals and OCI/eOCI cardholders must complete and submit the e-Arrival Card, a free service of Indian Immigration, and that it can be submitted online within 72 hours before arrival at boi.gov.in or indianvisaonline.gov.in or via the official 'Indian Visa Su-Swagatam' app. It says this is for arrival information, not a visa.

source.name: Indian Visa Online (Bureau of Immigration) — e-Arrival Card form ('It is free of cost service of Indian Immigration'); the 72-hour window is in the portal's home page notice

declarations.name: Air Suvidha Self-Declaration Form
declarations.text: The Air Suvidha portal says all international passengers arriving in India are required to submit a health self-declaration online through the portal before arrival. It says the form is free of cost, can be filled up to 72 hours before arriving, is mandatory under the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 and the Disaster Management Act, 2005, and that the registration number is presented at the health desk on landing.

currencyLimits.text: India's customs guide for travellers says you must declare to Customs on a Currency Declaration Form when foreign exchange exceeds USD 10,000 or its equivalent and/or foreign currency notes exceed USD 5,000 or equivalent, and that residents may carry INR 25,000 abroad. Canada's travel advice says non-residents are prohibited from importing or exporting the Indian rupee.

safety.text: The UK warns that scammers, pickpockets and ticket touts target foreign nationals in tourist areas, and that female travellers often experience verbal and physical harassment. The UK advises against all travel within 10 km of the Pakistan border and to Jammu and Kashmir (except travel by air to and within the city of Jammu), and against all but essential travel to Manipur.

bestTimeToVisit.text: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit. Canada's travel advice says the monsoon season extends from June to September and that heavy rain can cause flooding throughout the country; the UK's says the monsoon usually runs from June to November. Canada adds that India's coastline is subject to cyclones, particularly between April and December.

The UK government says UK drivers need both the 1949 version of the international driving permit (IDP) and their UK driving licence; Canada's travel advice says you must carry an International Driving Permit.

tips.text: The e-Visa portal's FAQ says https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/evisa/ is the only official website to apply for the e-Visa, and that no facilitation is required by any intermediary or travel agent.
The e-Visa portal says to print your Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) and present it at the immigration check post, where the eVisa will be stamped on your passport.

Canada's travel advice says special permits are required to visit certain parts of India designated as restricted or protected areas, and links to India's Bureau of Immigration for them. The e-Visa portal says an e-Visa is not valid for visiting protected, restricted and cantonment areas.
Canada's travel advice says eating or drinking unsafe food or water can make you sick, and gives the rule: boil it, cook it, peel it, or leave it.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for India?
faq.answer: Yes. India's visa portal says a valid passport and a regular visa, e-Visa or OCI card are required for entry, except for those exempted under bilateral arrangements, and the Bureau of Immigration lists visa-free entry only for citizens of Nepal, Bhutan and the Maldives. US citizens are on the e-Tourist Visa fee table (one month, one year or five years); the portal says to apply at least 4 days before arrival.

faq.question: How much does an India eVisa cost?
faq.answer: The portal's e-Tourist fee table lists, for most nationalities, USD 10 for the 30-day visa from April to June and USD 25 from July to March, USD 40 for one year and USD 200 for five years; some nationalities pay different amounts (US citizens USD 160 for five years) or nothing. A 3% bank transaction charge is added.

faq.question: How long does the India eVisa take?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states how long an e-Visa takes to process. The portal says e-Tourist and e-Business applications may be made at least 4 days before arrival and up to 120 days ahead, and that the fee must be paid at least 4 days before the expected date of travel.

faq.question: Do I need vaccinations to enter India?
faq.answer: Only in certain cases. India's Bureau of Immigration says anyone arriving from or transiting through a yellow fever endemic country by air or sea must hold a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate, and that those without one who have visited or transited such an area will be kept in quarantine for up to 6 days. WHO's country list says India requires proof of oral polio vaccination from resident national travellers arriving from certain polio-affected countries.

faq.question: Can I extend an India eVisa?
faq.answer: No. The e-Visa portal says e-Visas are non-extendable and non-convertible. The one-year and five-year e-Tourist Visas allow multiple entries, and the maximum stay in India during one calendar year should not exceed 180 days.
